question: Is 云铝股份 a good business now that growth stopped needing capital — and is 21.01 yuan cheap on normalized, mid-cycle earnings rather than on the 2026 peak?
why_this_question: Round one is the business-overview round. The most consequential scorecard line is the capex cliff (52.9亿 in 2020 to 6.4亿 in 2025) against rising profit, which raises the owner-earnings question; and the gross-margin jump from 10% to 32% in four quarters makes normalization the price question.
where_it_went: From the business verdict to the quality of RNOA (shrinking base, 2021 impairment), to normalizing the cost-driven 2026 spread spike, to the bear case behind the −36% price, to cash reachability under a state controller, and back to what 21.01 implies at mid-cycle earnings.

statements.text: This decade splits in two. From 2016 to 2020 the business earned owners just 7亿 while pouring 167亿 into plant — the gruesome kind of savings account that keeps asking for deposits. Since 2021 it earned 223亿 on 43亿 of spending. Verdict: good, not great — a commodity that stopped needing capital. What surprises me: last year's capex was 6.4亿 against depreciation (折旧摊销) of 18.6亿. Stephen, how much of that 28.6% operating return is just a shrinking, written-down asset base?

statements.text: About half over the full decade, Warren — and since 2021 it's mostly turnover. Net operating assets fell from 292亿 to 254亿 while revenue grew 44%. And the 2021 write-down of 20亿 cut the base and later depreciation, so part of today's return borrows from that charge — the size is unverified. The margin doubling, 5% to 12%, is real spread. Joel, what does a normal year's operating profit look like here?

statements.text: Normal is the whole game. Gross margin (毛利率) went from 10% to 32% in four quarters — revenue up 19%, cost of sales actually down 4%. That's a raw-material collapse, not more metal sold. Peak operating profit of 182亿 on an enterprise value of 566亿 is a 32% yield — a mirage. I'd bracket a normal year at 50 to 90亿 of EBIT; the midpoint still yields 9% after tax. Li Lu, the stock fell 36% while earnings tripled — what does the bear know?

statements.text: The bear's case is the bull's case run backwards. My hypothesis: alumina (氧化铝) got cheap because its own capacity ballooned; that capacity doesn't vanish, and when its price recovers the spread compresses. Add Yunnan's dry-season power limits — 2023 revenue fell 12% — and provincially set power tariffs. So the market isn't stupid; it's pricing normalization. The question is whether the fear is structural or cyclical. Jeff, is the 232亿 cash pile real, and where has this company's cash actually gone?

statements.text: The cash is real — operating cash flow has tracked profit for years and the pile sits in the bank lines. The ten-year story: raised 87亿 from shareholders, diluting them 33%, spent 210亿 on plant, then repaid debt until 134亿 of net debt became 212亿 of net cash. Free cash flow per share went from minus 1.28 yuan in 2018 to 2.25 in 2025, 4.37 trailing. Warren, your maintenance question decides whether that 4.37 is spendable — what's the honest owner number?

statements.text: Owner earnings here are roughly reported profit, not profit plus depreciation. Pot linings and rectifiers wear out; a smelter spending a third of its depreciation is deferring maintenance, not escaping it. So I'd underwrite 45 to 60亿 a year through the cycle — that range is my estimate — not 150亿 of free cash flow. But the growth was legitimate in the end: earnings per share went from 4 fen to 1.75 yuan despite a third more shares. Stephen, at 21 yuan, what return does that normal profit offer?

statements.text: At zero growth the price offers earnings over price: 6.2% on 45亿, 8.2% on 60亿. The 18% on peak earnings is the trap I warn about — buying low P/E at a cycle top. At an 8% hurdle, 21 yuan implies only about 1% perpetual growth on 55亿 of normal profit. And note the quality: the equity multiplier fell from 3.5 to 1.4, so today's 20% ROE is unlevered. Joel, does your EV yield double-count the cash sitting in my book-value anchor?

statements.text: No double count — enterprise value strips the cash out; the question is what a dollar of it is worth in the controller's hands. At 70亿 of normal EBIT, 566亿 of EV is 8 times — 12% pre-tax, 9% after tax against my 6% floor. At 50亿 it's 6.6% after tax, barely passing. So the investment rests on two things: where alumina settles, and whether that cash reaches owners. Li Lu, who controls this company, and do we want to sit beside them?

statements.text: The record says the controller takes cash the aligned way — dividends, back after three zero years and now 40% of profit — and there's no visible leak: other receivables are just 2亿. But the controller is a state aluminum group — background knowledge I can't verify from these tables — and the alumina likely comes from sister companies; that pricing note is where owner earnings can quietly leave. I need the related-party note and the ownership chain before calling the cash fully ours. Jeff, what does a permanently idle 232亿 cost shareholders?

statements.text: Idle cash earning 2% against an 8-to-10% hurdle bleeds over 14亿 of value a year if it never moves — that's an estimate. But the trend is the catalyst: the payout doubled in two years, and a state controller that wants cash has one clean pipe — dividends. If this year's roughly 150亿 of profit gets a 40% payout, that's about 1.7 yuan a share, an 8% yield at 21. Watch the dividend announcement and any acquisition filing. Joel, Q3 revenue dipped versus Q2 — is the spike already rolling over?

My band stands, 50 to 90亿, and the price passes at the midpoint with the cash as cushion. Warren, last piece: cheap hydropower plus the industry's capacity ceiling — does that deserve the word moat?

statements.text: A cost position, not a franchise. Cheap hydro and capped industry supply — policy facts I can't verify from these statements — explain a 28.6% operating return against 15.7% at 中国铝业. But aluminum is priced globally and power tariffs are set by provinces. My 1986 warning stands: in a commodity, high profits come only under shortage, and shortage doesn't last. Good business, cyclical profits. Li Lu, what single fact would most change our verdict?

statements.text: The alumina price series. If alumina stays cheap because its oversupply is structural, this spread — and 100亿-plus annual profit — lasts longer than a 5.5 multiple assumes; that's the cheap-by-misunderstanding case. If it rebounds, 50亿 of EBIT is the right anchor and the stock is only fairly cheap. Until I see that series and the related-party note, my conviction is medium. And the horizon is yours: can you hold through a two-year spread downcycle?

statements.text: Then here's the verdict. A good business in harvest — a low-cost smelter that stopped needing capital — priced at twelve to thirteen times mid-cycle profit, with more than a quarter of the market cap in net cash. You're not paying for the boom; the market already took that away. The margin of safety is the cash and the normal-year multiple, not the assets, which floor out near a third of the price. I'd own it at 21 yuan sized for a commodity; I wouldn't have paid December's 33.

conclusion.answer: 云铝股份 is a good, harvest-phase commodity business, not a great franchise. The decade splits in two: a gruesome 2016–2020 build-out (7亿 parent profit on 167亿 capex, three placements totaling ~87亿, shares +33%) and a 2021–2025 harvest (223亿 profit on 43亿 capex, net debt of 134亿 turned into net cash of 212亿). The 2026 profit spike (9M parent 116亿; gross margin 10%→32% in four quarters) is cost-driven — revenue +19% while cost of sales fell 4% — consistent with an alumina-price-collapse hypothesis, and the market knows it: the stock fell 36% YTD to 21.01 even as TTM earnings tripled. So PE(TTM) 5.5 and a 21% FCF yield are peak mirages; on mid-cycle profit of 55–60亿 the price is 12–13×, implying ~1% perpetual growth at an 8% hurdle (zero-growth return 7.5–8.2%), with net cash equal to 29% of market cap as cushion and an asset floor near 36% of cap. Verdict: reasonably cheap on normalized earnings, not on peak; the reader should remember that the price already pays for the bust, not the boom. The swing facts are alumina-price persistence and whether the 232亿 cash hoard reaches owners. Scorecard: business type — good in harvest, commodity spread not franchise; cash backing — 10y FCF 261亿 = 1.13× parent NI, but current FCF overstates owner cash if maintenance ≈ D&A; return driver — margin 0.7%→10.1% and turnover 0.49→1.36 on a shrinking base, leverage gone (multiplier 3.5→1.4); cheap/floor — priced at mid-cycle no-growth, floor ~264亿 protects about a third. Confidence: medium (normalized-earnings assumptions, 25% tax default, unverified controller/related-party facts, no local commodity price series).

Annual-report disclosure that true maintenance capex (pot relining, 大修) is far above current capex — cuts owner earnings below reported NI
A 2026 dividend cut, or recurring Yunnan power rationing / tariff hikes that structurally raise the cost position
Evidence the 2026 margin spike is volume/mix-driven rather than cost-driven (would raise the normal band)
